First, notice that $11!=11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot 8!\,.$ Then, we can cancel the $8!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{11!}{8!} & =\frac{11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot 8!}{8!} \\  & =\frac{11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot \cancel{8!}}{\cancel{8!}} \\  & =\frac{11\cdot 10\cdot 9}{1} \\  & =990\end{aligned}
$$
